title: Season 1, Ep 8: Edge AI deployment
oneliner: Cloud LLM calls bleed token cost - edge deployment moves models to your own environment, starting with model optimization.
says: Running LLMs on AWS, Azure, or IBM Cloud comes with a critical problem: token cost, which rises because you are using someone else's infrastructure and model. To avoid token cost and optimize with on-premises deployment, go for edge AI deployment. As an AI infrastructure architect you must know three major areas to deploy LLMs in your own environment - the first being model optimization.
explained: The economics here complete a triangle the season has been drawing: Episode 4 priced cloud inference through the gateway, Episode 7 moved hosting on-premises for control, and Episode 8 pushes models all the way to the edge - your own hardware, close to where data is generated - for cost and latency. The driver he names is token economics: per-call pricing is an operating expense that grows with success, while owned capacity is a fixed cost that flattens it.

Model optimization is correctly first on his list because edge hardware is constrained: quantization (shrinking model precision), distillation (smaller models taught by bigger ones), and pruning decide whether a useful model fits on the box at all. It is the inference economy from reel #22 expressed as an infrastructure decision - and it connects to the user's own interests, since this is exactly the arithmetic behind running LLMs on local hardware.
takeaway: When per-token cloud costs outgrow owned hardware, edge deployment wins - and model optimization is the skill that makes models fit.
